title: Detection of thermal shift in cellular Keap1 by protein-protein interaction inhibitors using immunoblot- and fluorescence microplate-based assays
protocol: Prepare the test compounds and thermocycler.
Set a water bath to 25°C for cell lysate preparation steps.
Warm the cell culture medium to 37°C.
Prepare stock solutions of compounds by dissolving them in an organic solvent suitable for the compound and diluting in cell culture medium at a concentration tolerated by the cells.
Pre-program two protocols on the thermal cycler, each with six temperature zones: one from 40°C to 52.5°C and another from 55°C to 67.5°C, followed by 25°C for 3 minutes in all cases.
Count HL-60 cells and adjust the cell density to 1–2 × 10^6 cells per mL.
Plate 15 mL of cell suspension into each of six separate T75 flasks.
Add 15 μL of vehicle [DMSO] to each of the first three flasks.
Add 15 μL of test compound [PRL-295 stock concentration: 10 mM, final concentration 10 μM] to each of the other three flasks.
Gently pipette the cell suspension to ensure homogeneous mixing.
Incubate the cells in a humidified 37°C with 5% CO2 incubator for a period of 1–3 h.
Transfer the cell suspensions from each treatment group into their respectively labeled 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 300 × g for 4 min at temperature between 20°C-25°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and gently flick the bottom of the tube to loosen the cell pellet before resuspending the cells in 20 mL of PBS.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 300 × g for 4 min at temperature between 20°C-25°C.
Wash the cells with PBS to remove serum present in the culture media.
Repeat steps 5.c and 5.d once more.
Prepare 10 mL of PBS supplemented with protease inhibitor cocktail (PBS-PIC).
Aspirate all supernatant carefully from centrifuged cells.
Gently resuspend cell pellet in each tube with 1.5 mL of PBS-PIC.
Ensure cell suspension is homogeneous without visible clumps.
Flick the tube gently to loosen the cell pellet before resuspending.
Aliquot 100 μL of cell suspension (∼1–2 million cells) into each of 12 separate PCR tubes.
Label the tubes according to their treatment and temperature (40°C–67.5°C, 2.5°C increments).
Start the program on the thermal cycler that you have set up previously.
Place the tubes in the thermocycler once the temperature has been reached for the first set of tubes (40°C–52.5°C, 2.5°C increments).
Remove the tubes from the PCR machine once the program has ended.
Let the tubes cool at a temperature between 20°C-25°C for a further 3 minutes.
Snap-freeze the tubes in liquid N2.
Repeat steps to place and process the next set of tubes with the second thermocycler program (55°C–67.5°C, 2.5°C increments).
Snap-freeze the tubes from the second set in liquid N2.
Wear protective goggles and gloves when transferring tubes from liquid N2.
Use forceps to transfer tubes from liquid N2 to prevent bodily injuries.
Obtain the soluble fraction from the heat-treated cells.
Place the tubes in a 96-well plastic float and transfer to a 25°C water bath to thaw.
Check the samples every minute until completely defrosted.
Vortex briefly with a few pulses once the lysates have thawed.
Repeat the freeze-thaw cycle three more times.
Transfer all the lysate (∼100 μL) from each tube into a labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the lysates at 17,000 × g for 40 min at 4°C.
Carefully place all tubes on ice after centrifugation ends.
Pipette 60 μL of the supernatant from each tube without touching the pellet and sides of the tubes.
Transfer 60 μL of lysate to a fresh centrifuge tube containing 20 μL of 4× LDS sample loading buffer and 4 μL of β-mercaptoethanol (β-ME).
Resolve the proteins in the soluble fractions using electrophoresis.
Load 13 μL of the samples into each well of a 26-well 4%-12% NuPAGE BT midi gel along with pre-stained molecular weight markers.
Use the NuPAGE midi gel running tank and NuPAGE 1× MOPS running buffer for loading.
Run the gel at 100 V for approximately 2 hours and 10 minutes.
Check the gel frequently during running to ensure proper separation of samples.
Stop the run once the LDS loading dye reaches the bottom of the gel.
Transfer resolved proteins from the gel to a nitrocellulose membrane.
Place the gel into the transfer sandwich cassette after completing the run.
Soak two pieces of Whatman 3MM filter paper and a sponge in transfer buffer at the cathode side.
Remove any bubbles trapped under the gel using a roller.
Pre-soak a 0.45-μm nitrocellulose membrane in transfer buffer.
Place the pre-soaked nitrocellulose membrane on top of the gel.
Use a roller to remove any bubbles between the gel and the membrane before securing the clasp.
Soak two pieces of filter paper and a sponge in transfer buffer for the anode side.
Place soaked filter papers and sponge on top of the nitrocellulose membrane.
Fit the transfer sandwich cassette in the Criterion Blotter transfer tank and insert an ice pack.
Fill the tank up with transfer buffer to the marked fill level.
Transfer at 70 V for 1 h 10 min at temperature between 20°C-25°C.
Place the NC membrane in a clean container containing deionized water to rinse the blot briefly.
Stain the NC membrane with Ponceau S stain and rinse with deionized water to visualize the transfer quality.
Wash the NC membrane with PBST for 3 min twice or until the stain has been completely removed.
Detect Keap1 on the membrane by immunoblotting.
Block the NC membrane in PBST-Milk for 1 h at temperature between 20°C-25°C.
Incubate the NC membrane for 16–20 h in the Keap1 primary antibody diluted 1:1,000 in PBST-Milk at 4°C.
Wash the NC membrane in PBST for 10 min and repeat this wash step twice.
Incubate the NC membrane in the Goat anti-Rat IRDye 800 secondary antibody diluted 1:20,000 in PBST-Milk for 1 h at temperature between 20°C-25°C, protected from light.
Wash the NC membrane in PBST for 10 min at temperature between 20°C-25°C, protected from light, and repeat this wash step two more times.
Scan the NC membrane using the Odyssey CLx scanner to visualize the bands corresponding to the Keap1 protein (∼65 kDa).
Measure the intensity of each band using Image StudioTM Lite software.
Export the data to an excel spreadsheet.
In each group, normalize the intensity of the bands by setting the 40°C treatment band intensity to 100%.
Plot the values relative to the 40°C treatment intensity to form aggregation curves for vehicle treated samples and compound treated samples.
Compare the two curves to observe differences in the thermostability profile of Keap1.
Treat HL-60 cells with 0.1% (v/v) DMSO or 10 μM PRL-295 for 3 hours.
Perform Keap1-CETSA assay using intact live HL-60 cells.
Obtain soluble fraction from treated cells.
Measure fluorescence intensity of Keap1 bands normalized to the 40°C treatment condition.
Plot data points for three replicates per condition.
Generate a sigmoidal curve using four parameter logistic (4PL) regression model.
Quantify the amount of Keap1 in each lane.
Obtain the fluorescence intensity of each band on the western blot image using the ‘Add Rectangle’ or ‘Draw Rectangle’ function found within the Analysis tab in the Image StudioTM Lite software.
Export the file or copy and paste the intensities from the ‘Shapes’ tab into a Microsoft Excel file.
Label the treatment and temperature conditions for each acquired band intensity.
Normalize the band intensity from each treatment to its respective 40°C temperature condition, setting the 40°C band intensity to 100%.
Plot the normalized band intensity of Keap1 at each temperature using Prism software.
Perform statistical analysis on the data.
Enter or import data into a new XY Table Format in Prism software.
Show the row titles and enter x values (Numbers) as [Temperatures (°C)].
Enter y values as 3 replicate values in side-by-side columns.
Plot relative band intensities calculated in Microsoft Excel on the y-axis from each temperature condition (x-axis) using Prism software.
Select the ‘Interpolate a standard curve’ option under Analysis in Prism.
Choose the ‘Sigmoidal, 4PL, X is log(concentration)’ equation with ‘No special handling for outliers’ and plot curve with ‘95% confidence bands’.
Compare means of treatment groups from each temperature condition by performing a Student’s t-test.
Wash each 15-cm dish thrice with PBS.
Aspirate the PBS and add 1 mL of PBS-PIC.
Scrape the cells from each dish with a cell lifter and collect into 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Pellet the cells at 400 × g for 5 min using a microcentrifuge.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving less than 10 μL in the tube.
Snap-freeze the tubes with the cell pellets in liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen tubes at -80°C until use.
Prepare PBS-PIC, using 1.5 mL per each cell pellet from a 15-cm dish.
Scale the PBS-PIC amount proportionally to the surface area of the dish if not using a 15-cm diameter.
Thaw the appropriate number of cell pellets required for the experiment size.
Add 1.5 mL of PBS-PIC to each tube and resuspend well.
Separate the mixture into two 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes, approximately 750 μL each.
Snap-freeze the tubes in liquid N2 and leave them in liquid N2 for at least 3 minutes.
Place the samples into a foam float or rack and transfer to a 25°C water bath.
Thaw the samples for 4–8 minutes until completely thawed.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Repeat steps three more times, vortexing each time after thawing.
Spin the tubes at 9,600 × g for 5 minutes between 20°C and 25°C.
Collect the supernatants and combine those from the same cell type together.
Separate supernatants into 650 μL aliquots, 3 aliquots of each cell type for each treatment or control.
Treat the cell lysates with compounds.

Prepare solutions of compounds of interest or vehicle such as DMSO in PBS at concentration that is 131-fold higher than the desired final concentration, with the final volume in excess of 30 μL for each type of treatment or control.
Mix 5 μL of the compound solution prepared previously, or 5 μL of vehicle solution, with the 650 μL cell lysate in triplicates, for both cell types.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 h.
Subject the treated cell lysates to heat treatment.
Separate each mixture into 12 of 50-μL aliquots, into either 0.2 mL PCR tubes or individual wells of MicroAmp Optical 96-well reaction plates cut to be compatible with the thermal cycler.
The pattern should correspond to the temperature zones in the thermal cycler to ensure that each aliquot from the same sample is heated at a different temperature.
Start one of the pre-programmed protocols on the thermal cycler and ensure that the temperature gradient has been established before placing the set of tubes into the preheated thermal cycler.
Remove the tubes/plate from the PCR machine once the program has ended.
Let the tubes cool at a temperature between 20°C-25°C for further 3 min.
Transfer the lysates into pre-labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 17,000 × g for 40 min at 4°C.
Move the tubes onto ice and transfer 40 μL of each lysate into a separate well of a 96-well clear plate.
Do not touch the pellet and the side of the tube with the pelleted lysates.
Fill white flat-bottom 96-well plates with 65 μL of PBS-PIC for KC-lysates or 85 μL of PBS-PIC for C-lysates in a desired pattern.
Include a row of “blanks” with 100 μL of PBS-PIC.
For all rows except the last one, add 65 μL of PBS-PIC and 35 μL of indicated sample for KC-lysates.
For all rows except the last one, add 85 μL of PBS-PIC and 15 μL of indicated sample for C-lysates.
Add 100 μL of PBS-PIC to the last row.
Transfer 35 μL of lysate from “holding” plates to pre-filled white 96 well plates for KC-lysates.
Transfer 15 μL of lysate from “holding” plates to pre-filled white 96 well plates for C-lysates.
Set up the plate reader.
Select Fluorescence tab within Settings: Excitation 580 nm, Cut off 590 nm, Emission 615 nm.
In Plate tab, select “96-well standard opaque”.
Place the white plate into the plate drawer on top of an adaptor frame for 96-well plates.
Measure the mCherry fluorescence of the entire plate or in selected wells.

Subtract the background calculated as an average fluorescence values of all PBS-PIC samples (“blanks”) from all other values in the same plate to get the background-corrected fluorescence values for the samples.
For each cell type, calculate the average background-corrected fluorescence of vehicle-treated samples heated at 39°C to get a normalization factor.

Normalize the data by dividing each background-corrected fluorescence value by the normalization factor specific for each cell type. Use the same normalization factor for vehicle and compound-treated cells of the same type.
Plot the normalized data against the heating temperature.
Optionally, fit the local polynomial regression curve to the data using R or other suitable software.
Enhance visualization by adding smoothing lines that represent local polynomial regressions fitted to the data.
